dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Are the two of you... here to train Fungi as well?

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: #Even with the ability to take down thousands of bandits single-handedly, {NICKNAME} still continues to train and work as hard as ever... That really does put a lot of pressure on your opponents!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, now that you mention it, how are you speaking so fluently now? Is it because you're not scared of us anymore?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Erm... Uh... Ahem... Umm...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Even though I have the utmost respect for you two, that doesn't mean I'm scared to talk to you.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: You're not the reason I was stuttering before... It's a little complicated.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows why! You're afraid of Miko because you always miss your submission deadlines!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you tremble with anxiety when you're reminded of an impending deadline whenever Miko is standing next to you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *whimper* There's so much work...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: P—Please keep your voice down!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Even if you were right, you didn't have to say it out loud...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, our lips are sealed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, good luck, Souka!

choices.text: What kind of weird nicknames are these...?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Ahh, do you not like them?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: The authors occasionally talk about you guys when they eat. They would come up with nicknames for you guys, and there would always be a nickname or two that could receive a standing ovation...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon actually finds it pretty interesting. The nicknames that the authors came up with really are something. They have just the right vibe for important characters in a novel!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Souka, are you gonna name your Fungus something similar as well? Paimon remembers you were the one that named Miko's Fungus, right?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: To be honest, I was planning on naming it something more casual.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: However, Lady Yae said, "Since you're writing a passionate and intense novel, you should break free from all restraints and be as hyperbolic as necessary."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The mercenaries seem to be doing the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, you're right. The nicknames the mercenaries gave Paimon and {NICKNAME} do sound pretty ridiculous!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Golden Comet is crashing down——boom! And Silver Companion is close behind with a combo——ba-bam!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: It's said that a "name" is an expression of anticipation. It allows people and things to move toward what the "name" means.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If the Fungus is named something cool, maybe it'll grow into something really powerful!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Then Paimon will have to call out Bongo-Head's name more frequently!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That way, Bongo-Head's head will actually go "bing bong" when Paimon knocks on it later.

choices.text: I still think it'll sound more like a squelch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, care to make a bet!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoever loses needs to let Bongo-Head ride on their back for three days!

choices.text: "Bing bong" is the sound when you hit someone with a Mist Bubble.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Thank you. I know they're just ordinary words of encouragement, but I feel so honored!

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Hey, you two! Are you here to train your Fungi as well?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Everything's going great! My Ace Fungus Stormstress is performing spectacularly.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I've relied almost solely on Stormstress for the entire preliminary round. It also helped me realize that there are weaknesses in my team.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Yep, a story's climax or a protagonist's fall will only make sense if you tell the reader about the underlying issues ahead of time.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: That's pretty much what the preliminary round means to a beast tamer like me.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Looking at it from this perspective, Stormstress has been extremely important to me! It's like a classic companion of any protagonist!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Souka is in the zone all of a sudden... She's amazing!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Umm... to be honest... there hasn't been any progress outside of the competition itself...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Lady Yae said that now that I've signed up for the competition, my priority should be to adopt a beast-tamer mentality and get into character as fast as I can.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If I can do that, I'll be able to find new ideas for my piece in each and every round I go into.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: However, even though the main storyline of the novel is about a competition and each round serves as an important chapter... there are still blanks in between the chapters that need to be filled with daily life and subplots.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: All I have right now is an outline that doesn't include the daily life stuff... I have no idea how to refine it.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If I were to travel around sightseeing with Lady Yae... Maybe I'd be able to find some inspiration!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Won't you be too nervous?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it feels like you're too nervous to even speak when Miko's around. Would you be able to sleep if you were to travel with her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon bets you wouldn't even be able to hold your utensils straight if the two of you had to eat together.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: What? You're exaggerating! You know, I'm not always in fear of Lady Yae rushing my writing!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Ahem... anyway, as a novelist, traveling with Lady Yae is the happiest and most honorable thing I could do! The inspiration that I'd be able to find would last me years!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Thank you so much! I can feel the motivation rising inside me!

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: *sob*... What am I gonna do... I put in the time and prepared as best I could... But I was still defeated in just the second round!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, don't be too hard on yourself, Souka. Don't worry, Miko won't blame you!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: You guys... even at a time like this... you two are still here to comfort me. Do I even deserve this special honor...?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Wait... hold on! Ideas are growing inside my head... Spectacular arcs and subplots are appearing on their own!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Don't say anything... Let me guess... you're about to say...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: "I've witnessed your courage and determination! I will fulfill your wish and claim victory on your behalf!"

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Perfect! I know how the story goes from here! I'll pair this with the accidental encounter with the strongest opponent from before! I have to remember it for now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just as Miko said. Souka will return to normal after talking to herself...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Should we cheer as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shh, let's not disturb Souka right now. Let her sort out the thoughts in her head first!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If the protagonist were to encounter an immediate setback right at the start of the competition... The novel would separate itself from cliche tropes. It'll be both unexpected and exciting...

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Where could Lady Yae be...? Could it be that the routes I've chosen are too boring?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Yeah! Miss Aratani has no idea either... Do you guys know where Lady Yae went?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's going on? We heard that you guys left with someone that looked like a mercenary. Did you guys split up?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Mercenary? Oh, you mean the guide from the Corps of Thirty? We were just asking for directions to some famous local restaurant.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: The mercenary left after we arrived at the restaurant. Lady Yae was interested in the spices they used in the dishes and wanted to bring some back as souvenirs. So she went to look for a spice shop afterward...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But she's been gone for a whole three hours now!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's only been three hours...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, you scared Paimon there... You made it sound as if Miko's been missing for a really long time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe she saw something interesting and stuck around to take a closer look. There's no need to panic!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But we only have so much time on this trip to Sumeru, and I want to spend as much time with Lady Yae as possible! I want to learn as much as I can from her...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Sometimes, a simple comment of hers can be extremely insightful to an inexperienced writer like me. This is a rare opportunity!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Just now, for instance, I felt a kind of... hostile vibe from the mercenary that showed us the way. He kept looking at us as if he was planning on robbing us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to be scared, it's not like you did anything wrong! That mercenary was probably just on patrol. It would make sense to take notice of everyone around you when you're patrolling.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I'm not scared! But it seems like Lady Yae already noticed that he was watching us and said quietly to me, "If you suspect that someone's watching you, this is something you can do to turn the tables..."

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Lady Yae then called out to the mercenary and asked him to be our guide! The mercenary looked dumbfounded but quickly agreed to her request.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: The mercenary was nowhere to be seen again after taking us to the restaurant. I think it might've been because Lady Yae messed up his plans, and he was scared of making any bold moves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... you can do that?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Isn't Lady Yae so cool!? I'm gonna add this to my novel——

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Actively engaging with someone you suspect of following you... Disrupt their plans and force an unexpected change in their scheme to buy yourself more time...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But where does the story go from there? What if they return? Lady Yae said that she was going to buy some spices, but what if she secretly went to track the mercenary instead?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I think I've got it! This is the classic, take your opponent by surprise and checkmate them before they can react! Bring the fight to them while they're rallying and making adjustments!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Hmm? That means I have nothing to worry about!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: As expected of Lady Yae. I'm getting so excited just thinking about it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, but now Paimon is also curious about who that mercenary is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's ask Miko when we get a chance.

choices.text: The mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty are good people...
We'll go look for her as well...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: That would be great! If you find Lady Yae, please remind... I mean... suggest that she quickly return and meet up with us! I still have many things I'd like to ask her about!

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Magnificent! The match between you two and Miss Layla was intense but not hostile. This is exactly what a friendly match should look like!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Layla would be really happy to hear that!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I didn't know how to portray a character that's the protagonist's competitor... but then turned into the protagonist's friend instead. But I have a very clear idea about it now!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I need to think about the structure of the story and add a character like that for the protagonist!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Our match was friendly as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we were pretty relaxed when we were up against Souka as well. There was no anxiety or hostility either.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I know that you guys took it easy on me... but treating someone as ordinary as I am with such kindness... I don't even know how to thank the two of you!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Hmm, I'm gonna have to make some edits after I add this arc to the novel... It might be too much for the reader to handle if I were to disqualify the protagonist's rival... The tone needs to be a little more serious!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Miko lost, what a shame!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Huh? Didn't Lady Yae lose on purpose?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: She's probably more interested in the story of the gathering of the beast tamers —I wonder what kind of development would satisfy her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... you're right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she was clearly getting to Haniyyah... A few more words and she would've been able to set Haniyyah straight...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: That's probably because Lady Yae felt like her role wasn't the one that's supposed to be the close friend to Haniyyah in this story. She didn't want to steal your spotlight!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Besides, seeing how things have developed, maybe Lady Yae finds this to be "the perfect place to end the chapter"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't understand any of this writer lingo...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Sure! Keep up the good work! I'm looking forward to watching you guys in the finals!

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Ahh! No one could've expected such a great event to have such a jaw-dropping conspiracy behind it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the conspiracy has been dealt with! There's no need to be afraid!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, shouldn't Souka be shouting something like "Oh! I know what to add to my novel now!" at a time like this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is sure you found a ton of inspiration in such a drastic turn of events!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: To be honest... things kinda got out of hand and completely exceeded my expectations! More details and background must be added right from the beginning for a villain like Elchingen.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: It seems like you and Lady Yae noticed something was off a long time ago. Someone ordinary like me didn't have the slightest clue about what was going on.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If I'm going to add this to the novel, I'm gonna have to think real hard about how to build up the underlying mystery and slowly feed the reader different clues! It would be a little strange if the twist came too abruptly.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: However, the arc where the villain is defeated by the protagonist has to be perfect! I'll try drinking two pots of wine when I get writer's block!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: It's a method Lady Yae recommended. I'm gonna try it tonight!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Just make sure you don't drink too much... You might scare yourself with the things you end up writing!

choices.text: I'll leave you to your thoughts...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Huh!? Are you guys leaving already? I'll be sure to thank you properly when I get the chance!
